meaning: The Ursino-Lodi autoregulation sigmoid inputs are clamped to ±40 before exponentiation, so the sigmoid saturates instead of overflowing when flow deviates far from nominal. This bounds both the compliance-range switch dC and the sigmoid argument G*x/(dC/4).

could_move.what: Autoregulated arterial compliance C_a and its rate dCa_dt saturate at the clamp edge, so fitted P.G and P.tau can shift
dC switch is frozen at dCn or dCp once |10x| > 40, i.e. beyond ~0.4% flow deviation, which is very tight and may be doing more than overflow protection
Intracranial pressure dPic depends on C_a and dCa_dt, so clamped autoregulation changes the ICP trace
Jugular compression decks drive large flow deviations, exactly the regime where the clamp binds

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: during compression the autoregulation response is capped rather than growing, so C_a excursions and the ICP response are likely smaller than an unclamped model would give. The 10x clamp at ±40 binds at much smaller flow deviations than the ±40 on the G term, so it is the more suspicious of the two.

check.why: Solve and replot one jugular compression case, the regime where the clamp is most likely active, and inspect the C_a and Pic traces for flat saturated segments.
